title: Synthesis of CFET Cell Library Leveraging Backside Metal Routing
problem: Complementary FET (CFET) technology stacks PMOS and NMOS vertically, reducing routing tracks and increasing routing complexity; current synthesis lacks backside metal (BS) routing utilization and transistor folding efficiency.
motivation: CFET is a promising next-generation technology, but reduced routing resources and multi-level complexity require new cell synthesis strategies to maintain routability.
method: The approach leverages metal routing on both the backside and frontside of the chip to pack transistors more efficiently. Euler path analysis, a graph-based optimization method, determines the minimum spacing between transistor gates (contacted poly pitch); dynamic programming then calculates the number of routing channels required on the frontside. A mathematical constraint solver finalizes exact transistor placement and routing.
key_novelty: This is the first cell-synthesis approach to combine backside metal routing with efficient transistor folding (arranging transistors in space-saving patterns), using Euler path analysis and dynamic programming.
contributions: First work to utilize backside routing resources in CFET cell synthesis stage
Euler path-based lower bound estimation for contacted poly pitch
Dynamic programming-based FMRT calculation for BS-aware placement
SMT-based device placement and routing completion
1% CPP reduction, 45% M2 track reduction, 19% runtime reduction vs prior work
baselines: prior CFET cell synthesis without backside routing
limitations: Limited to standard cell library synthesis; full chip routing integration and power analysis not discussed.
